Information since May points to a strong labor market and solid growth, with inflation near 2%. The FOMC’s hike to 1.75–2% and guidance of further “gradual” increases, alongside “balanced” risks, still signals confidence in sustained expansion and anchored expectations. However, the April 2018 Senior Loan Officer Opinion Survey indicates some tightening through bank credit channels: banks reported wider loan rate spreads, policy changes in commercial real estate lending (pointing to tighter CRE credit conditions), and mixed CRE loan demand, while standards for qualified-mortgage jumbo loans were unchanged. Foreign banks reported demand and borrower inquiries for C&I and CRE loans, suggesting pockets of resilience. Netting these, the tone remains positive but is modestly tempered by signs of firmer bank lending terms, especially in CRE.
